de.name: Swanage Railway

en.name: Swanage Railway

en.name: Swanage Pier
en.text: A classic Victorian pier offering stunning views of Swanage Bay, popular for strolls, diving, and boat trips to Poole.

en.name: Swanage Beach
en.text: A gently sloping sandy beach with clean waters, ideal for families and offering traditional seaside activities and beach huts.

en.name: Durlston Country Park
en.text: A spectacular nature reserve and clifftop park offering panoramic sea views, diverse habitats, and a gateway to the Jurassic Coast.

en.name: Durlston Castle

en.name: Wellington Clock Tower

en.name: Swanage Museum & Heritage Centre

en.name: St Mary's Church

en.name: Peveril Point
en.text: A rocky headland offering dramatic views of the coastline, known for its treacherous waters and as a popular spot for birdwatching.

en.name: Prince Albert Gardens
en.text: A tiered landscaped garden overlooking the bay, providing a peaceful space for relaxation and hosting local community events.

en.name: The Mowlem

en.name: Old Harry Rocks
en.text: Iconic chalk formations standing at the eastern end of the Jurassic Coast, accessible via a scenic walk from Swanage.

descriptionAdvanced.de: Swanage liegt am östlichen Ende der Isle of Purbeck in Dorset und ist Teil des UNESCO-Welterbes Jurassic Coast. Ursprünglich ein kleiner Fischerort, entwickelte sich Swanage im 19. Jahrhundert zu einem bedeutenden Zentrum für den Abbau und Export von Purbeck-Stein und Purbeck-Marmor, der in vielen englischen Kathedralen verwendet wurde. Mit dem Bau der Eisenbahn im Jahr 1885 transformierte sich der Ort in ein beliebtes viktorianisches Seebad. Ein besonderes Highlight ist die heute museumsbahnähnlich betriebene Swanage Railway, die historische Dampf- und Dieselzüge durch die malerische Landschaft nach Corfe Castle führt. Die Stadt zeichnet sich durch ihren sanft abfallenden Sandstrand und das klare Wasser der Swanage Bay aus. Kulturell ist der Ort für seine Festivals bekannt, darunter das Jazz Festival und das Folk Festival. Die Geologie der Umgebung mit den Klippen von Old Harry Rocks bietet spektakuläre Ausblicke auf den Ärmelkanal.
descriptionAdvanced.hu: Swanage Dorset megyében, a Purbeck-félsziget keleti csücskén fekszik, és az UNESCO Világörökség részét képező Jurakori part egyik ékköve. A település története szorosan összefügg a bányászattal: a híres Purbeck-mészkövet és márványt évszázadokon át innen szállították Londonba és a nagy angol katedrálisok építéséhez. A 19. században George Burt és John Mowlem vállalkozók munkássága nyomán vált népszerű tengerparti üdülőhellyé, számos viktoriánus stílusú épülettel gazdagodva. A város egyik legnagyobb vonzereje a Swanage Railway, egy önkéntesek által működtetett nosztalgia gőzvasút, amely Corfe Castle váráig közlekedik. A Swanage-öböl védett, homokos strandja kiváló fürdőhely, miközben a környék sziklái, mint például az Old Harry Rocks, a természetjárók paradicsoma. A város gazdasága ma is a turizmusra, a kézműves iparra és a kulturális fesztiválokra támaszkodik.
descriptionAdvanced.ro: Swanage este o stațiune litorală pitorească situată în comitatul Dorset, în extremitatea estică a Insulei Purbeck. Orașul face parte din Coasta Jurasică, sit aflat în patrimoniul mondial UNESCO, datorită geologiei sale unice. Istoria locală a fost dominată timp de secole de industria pietrei, piatra de Purbeck fiind extrasă din carierele din apropiere și folosită la construcția unor edificii majore precum Catedrala Salisbury sau Westminster Abbey. În epoca victoriană, Swanage s-a transformat într-o destinație de vacanță rafinată, proces accelerat de sosirea căii ferate în 1885. Astăzi, linia ferată Swanage Railway este operată ca o atracție turistică cu locomotive cu abur, oferind călătorii nostalgice prin peisajul rural. Plaja cu nisip fin și apele liniștite ale golfului Swanage atrag mii de turiști anual. De asemenea, orașul este renumit pentru viața sa culturală vibrantă, găzduind festivaluri de jazz, folk și blues în fiecare an.
descriptionAdvanced.en: Swanage is a coastal town and civil parish in the south-east of Dorset, England, situated at the eastern end of the Isle of Purbeck. It is a key gateway to the Jurassic Coast, a UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for its unique geological formations. Originally a small fishing port, Swanage rose to prominence as a center for the quarrying and shipping of Purbeck stone and marble, which has been utilized in grand architecture across Britain since Roman times. During the 19th century, the town was developed into a fashionable seaside resort by local businessmen John Mowlem and George Burt, who incorporated architectural fragments from London into the town's fabric. The Swanage Railway, a preserved heritage line, is a major attraction, running steam-hauled trains to Corfe Castle. The town's sheltered bay offers safe swimming and diving, while the nearby chalk stacks of Old Harry Rocks mark the easternmost point of the Jurassic Coast. Modern Swanage thrives on tourism, festivals, and its historical maritime heritage.
